correctness.rationale: For the stated itinerary, the opposite speeds on each interface force nonzero b_j of the same sign and b_C D,b_C E>0. Equality of each outer section Hamiltonian gives the reflection at r or ℓ, each with derivative −1. Central conservation gives AD=BE and K+(b_C/2)(D²−E²)=0. If A=B=0, the second relation alone determines a local smooth curve because E≠0; if A=B≠0 the curve is D=E with K=0. In either case each matched output near the given orbit equals the actual first hit by transversality and local uniqueness of the matching equation in the terminal ordinate. Positive residence and interior strip passage persist locally, so neither curve is consistent with an isolated cycle. Hence A/B>0 and A≠B; eliminating E gives the recorded algebraic reconstruction, not a converse existence test. Central first-hit derivatives are input normal speed over output normal speed. Their product with the two reflections gives the displayed positive μ. Substitution E=AD/B makes μ−1 equal to (A−B) times 2 b_C D (A+B)/[B(B−b_C E)(A+b_C D)], a strictly negative factor. Thus no neutral isolated cycle. No spectral assumption is needed. The verification phrase about time reversal should say it negates both offsets, reversing their inequality, not literally swapping their values; reoriented signed gaps also negate and the multiplier is the reciprocal. Independent `python3 /workspace/review_reproduction.py 2` used augmented affine matrix exponentials and root-bracketed section hits on the stated example: return slopes 7.163689820 and 0.139592864 versus formula 7.163689825 and reciprocal 0.139592867. These finite numerical checks corroborate the example, not the general proof.

evidence: The published two-zone theorem requires a single switching line with no sliding. Three-zone existence/uniqueness works emphasize the number of cycles, not the offset multiplier. The catalogue theorem covers center/saddle spectra and the same crossing order and local conditions.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A one-interface theorem cannot be applied twice to deduce a fixed point multiplier of this two-interface orbit. Cycle cardinality alone cannot rule out an isolated neutral fixed point. In contrast, the catalogue theorem is exactly applicable after the c_j-only perturbation described above; it imposes no change to the actual local return map.

originality.rationale: Distinct Resultary record ce433742339f states the same transverse multiplier, hyperbolicity and coefficient-only sign on the nondegenerate strips. The seemingly larger degenerate scope of the frozen result is implied: perturb only the three c_j while preserving all four local first-hit maps exactly. Indeed both endpoints of every flight have x²=1, so subtracting terminal from initial H_j deletes −c_j x²/2. Normal velocities and the local implicit branches at the output are unchanged as c_j varies slightly, and the genuine transverse hits persist on those branches. Thus the return map and isolation are identical after perturbation, not merely a limit of hyperbolic multipliers. All b_j≠0 make simultaneous nondegeneracy achievable by arbitrarily small perturbations of c_j. The covered theorem then gives the original claim verbatim after the gap-sign conversion. This is mathematical coverage, not a conclusion about publication priority or which record was written first. No old inaccessible article is used to justify the verdict.
residual_risks: The dates of the catalogue and frozen records do not settle historical priority.

value.rationale: A coefficient-only hyperbolicity test for this itinerary is intrinsically useful. But the mathematical conclusion and multiplier are already present in the equivalent catalogue theorem. Neither a change of gap signs, algebraic elimination to get the amplitude, nor including spectrally degenerate fields with an unchanged return map leaves a separately needed new invariant or substantive boundary theorem to repair.
